newsitem.title: USA: NYC expected to sue tobacco industry.
newsitem.headline: NYC expected to sue tobacco industry.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani is holding a news conference at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Thursday to announce that the city will sue the tobacco industry, said the Coalition for a Smoke-Free City.
A spokesperson for Guiliani confirmed there would be a news conference regarding the filing of a lawsuit but would not say if it was against the tobacco industry.
The coalition, which consists of New York's major health groups, has been urging the mayor to file suit due to inaction by New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco.

"The tobacco cartel has lied and misled the public about the dangers of tobacco addiction for decades. New York City's health care bill attributed to tobacco addiction exceeds $2 billion annually," the coalition said in a letter to Giuliani.
"Recovering these costs from the tobacco cartel would be popular, fair and a major boost to the City's treasury," it said.
If filed, the suit is expected to be similar to those brought by 16 states in an attempt to recoup health care costs of smokers.
San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Jose and 10 other counties in California have also sued the industry.

If New York City takes action, it will be the first city on the east coast to do so. Erie County, which includes the city of Buffalo, previously said it expects to file a Medicaid suit shortly and has been attempting to get other New York counties to join with it.

A source close to the city said the suit was expected to be filed Thursday morning in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan. It is expected to name major tobacco companies and two trade organizations as defendants.

"New York (would be) not only the largest city to file, it's larger than most of the states that have filed," said Richard Daynard, chairman of the Tobacco Products Liablity Project at Northeastern University in Boston.
"A public official today cannot refrain from collecting available funds for defraying this expense," Daynard said about health care costs related to smoking.
